title: Recurring global hooks
location: User-level hook adapter → common hook runner
note: A hook running is not a lesson delivered. Normal checks stay quiet; useful context is bounded, deduplicated and attributable to its trigger.
current: Source installs one light machine-wide hook set (session start, prompt, Bash pre-tool, stop, session end; Cursor adds post-tool, its only mid-turn message channel; Codex defers SessionEnd by name) into each installed harness's user config from setup, project install and refresh, and the per-hook self-heal; uninstall removes it and doctor reports it as HC-machine-hooks. Inside a project the user-level invocation steps aside when the project config owns the native event, tool events included, so one Yoke evaluation and one composed delivery run per event. Codex trusts only Yoke's own user-level handlers. Guard scope, yoke (<hook>): diagnostics and quiet success are unchanged. Required context retains its owners and structured delivery stays bounded; deployed harness proof is pending. SessionStart accepts every start source on all harnesses; Codex includes fork, clear and compact. Codex starts without a transcript path stop before relay and registration, regardless of source; prompt fallback registers only saved transcripts; an unclaimed turn with unavailable evidence ends quietly. Refresh renews Codex hook trust after content changes.
desired: Use machine guards outside projects; defer to project-owned events and preserve required bounded teaching.
